title: Hand-Coded String Formatting in Loops (Premature String Capacity)
pattern: Manually computing exact byte lengths and calling `.reserve()` on every iteration of a string concatenation loop to prevent reallocations.
why_bad: Rust's `String` growth algorithm uses a highly optimized geometric reallocation strategy. Manually calculating offsets and calling reserve inside the loop introduces extra branch evaluations and variable updates that slow down the code compared to straightforward concatenation [317, 360].
detection: Iterative call sequences containing explicit manual length calculations and calls to `.reserve()` directly inside string assembly loops.
counterexample: Allocating a single bulk reservation *before* entering the loop (`output.reserve(expected_total)`) which is highly efficient. `Context-dependent`.
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 20 (p. 317); *Code Complete*, Section 26.4 (p. 360).
